- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early days of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot the true price trajectory, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history.
- Model underreacts to recent downward trends in history, failing to adjust forecasts downward even when history shows clear mean reversion.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in capturing the true price’s upward momentum, especially in the 10–20 day range.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices — overconfidence in continuation of trend.
- Forecasts often fail to account for volatility clustering — underestimating sharp corrections after spikes.
- Model tends to underestimate the true price’s final 5–10 days, especially when the trend is accelerating upward.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 1–3% for the first 5 days if history shows recent upward momentum.
- If the last 5 days of history show a clear upward trend, reduce forecast peak by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If the true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in the last 5 days, adjust next forecast downward by 1–2% to reflect mean reversion.
